page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the c3 server family. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the x86_64 architecture and features an L3 cache size of 105 MB. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but weaker multi-core scaling. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores 1618.89, which is in the average range, while the multi-core score drops to 3315.66, falling into the weak category. Similarly, the Geekbench single-core score is 1713.0, whereas the multi-core score is 3813.0. Memory bandwidth is relatively low, with uncached large-block read speeds at 28.42 GB/sec and write speeds at 21.13 GB/sec. However, the instance performs moderately well in cryptographic and compression tasks, achieving average ratings in Passmark CPU encryption and single-threaded gzip compression.

The c3-standard-4 offers a balanced resource allocation profile for general-purpose workloads, but its lower multi-core efficiency and weak memory bandwidth present performance tradeoffs for highly parallelized or memory-intensive applications. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that rely on single-threaded execution or moderate throughput, such as static web serving, which reaches 6.68 GB/sec, and lightweight text processing. It is also suitable for small-scale language model text generation, achieving 112.11 tokens/sec on a 135M model, but is less optimal for heavy database operations, software compilation, or complex physics simulations.
